hypotheses.title: Ancestry-preserving prefix-cache admission with ghost hashes
hypotheses.mechanism: Under local KV pressure, retain complete reusable prefix blocks and decline optional cache writes for an unproven private suffix. Record each declined block's exact hash and parent hash in a bounded metadata-only ghost table. If the block is recomputed on a later request, promote it only after its parent is resident and all required cache groups can commit it. Once one block is declined, decline its descendants for that trajectory until a later request rebuilds the contiguous admission frontier. Active generation KV remains allocated normally.
hypotheses.nearest_prior_art: The open #51981 PR supplies request-level no-store; RR-Evict proposes tail-first reclamation for agent histories; open #54625 and #58837 reorder waiting-request admission; PEEK proposes queue-informed protection. A write-admission policy at the contiguous block frontier is a narrower adaptation. None of these sources proves a gain on the target deployment.
hypotheses.new_adaptation: Add bounded ghost metadata and a per-trajectory admission frontier at completed-block commit. Promote only after a repeat exact hash is observed through recomputation. Treat the cache-group bundle as the admission unit: publish a prefix hit only after every required group has committed the same complete token span. For asynchronous commits, use a completion fence and generation identifier before publishing; cancellation or speculative rollback invalidates pending writes and ghost observations from uncommitted tokens. If the pinned cache manager cannot provide this lifecycle, disable the policy for that configuration.
hypotheses.code_surface: V1 block-pool commit and eviction hooks, hybrid KV-cache group coordinator, asynchronous cache-commit completion, and per-run cache accounting. Exact pinned-file locations remain unknown.
hypotheses.online_policy: Observable state: completed exact block hashes with parent hashes, ghost repeat counts, free-block pressure, active-block pins, and group commit status. Decision rule: with ample free blocks, use stock admission; under pressure, retain the contiguous proven prefix and place newly computed private suffix blocks on metadata-only probation. On later recomputation, admit repeated blocks in ancestor order if every required group has capacity. Action: change optional local cache retention only. Overhead: bounded host hash-table updates and commit checks. Fallback: stock admission when metadata, group, or async guarantees are unavailable. Strongest static comparator: application-supplied #51981-style request no-store, alongside stock admission and RR-Evict at equal KV capacity.
hypotheses.strongest_objection: Declining a suffix may discard precisely the block needed on the next agent turn; ghost metadata cannot supply its KV and promotion requires recomputation. The extra policy may lose to simple request no-store or tail-first eviction, and no supplied B200 block trace establishes avoidable eviction.

novelty.deployment: Unestablished for B200 DEP8 or two DEP4. The 75% cacheability target is not a measured hit rate.
novelty.implementation: Proposed block-frontier write behavior differs from #51981's request-level switch, subject to inspection of the pinned cache lifecycle and overlap with existing policies.
novelty.publication: Unestablished; cache admission, tail eviction, and queue-informed protection have close prior art.

hypotheses.confidence: Moderate in the cache invariant and plausible failure mode; low in workload benefit.
hypotheses.readiness: Low-to-moderate for a CPU lifecycle prototype; low for serving integration until pinned hybrid-group and asynchronous-commit semantics are resolved.

evidence.quote: A request can still reuse existing prefix-cache entries, but newly computed blocks from that request are not admitted
evidence.claim: Request-level no-store is an existing comparator.

evidence.claim: The abstract motivates retaining contiguous agent prefixes under pressure; it does not validate this admission rule.

evidence.claim: Promotion must wait for a complete recomputed block.

evidence.claim: Cold-request TTFT and scheduler overhead remain necessary checks for cache-aware alternatives.

rubric.value: Conditional reduction in recomputed prompt tokens and TTFT tails for repeated agent histories; no target gain established.
rubric.mechanism: Bounded ghost hashes guide optional writes at a contiguous, complete-block cache frontier.
rubric.evidence: Agent-cache and request no-store sources support the opportunity and comparator; target eviction behavior is unknown.
rubric.integration: Hybrid group atomicity, asynchronous publication, and rollback make integration nontrivial.
rubric.correctness: A hit must reference a contiguous committed ancestry across every required group; active KV, cancellation, and speculative rollback must remain safe.
rubric.experiment: Use a small block-lifecycle test, then CPU replay of frozen request hashes and capacity; promote only if recomputed tokens improve against static controls.
rubric.cost: Low CPU-screen cost; serving integration and GPU cost unestimated.
rubric.distinctness: Changes local cache write admission, separate from request-level no-store, queue ordering, and eviction order.
rubric.research_contribution: Potential workload-specific policy study; publication novelty unestablished.

experiment.control: Stock admission, #51981-style request no-store, and RR-Evict-style tail eviction at equal effective KV capacity and identical request order.
experiment.treatment: Ghost-hash probation with ancestry-preserving promotion; keep checkpoint, precision, sampler, cache preparation, and active backend fixed within each topology.
experiment.measurements: Exact per-run hit and recomputed prompt tokens, evictions, scheduler CPU time, HBM occupancy, TTFT tails, TPOT, throughput, cost per token, and agent/tool quality; report DEP8 and two DEP4 separately across relevant concurrency.
experiment.reject_if: The lifecycle test violates contiguous group commits, CPU replay does not reduce recomputation against the strongest static control, or matched serving loses after scheduler cost.
experiment.correctness: Exercise shared and divergent prefixes, incomplete blocks, asynchronous completion, cancellation, speculative rollback, group mismatch, and output/logprob parity at fixed precision and sampling.
experiment.cost: CPU component test and replay first; matched serving cost remains unestimated. No GPU work was performed.

hypotheses.revision_after_critique: Explored request-level no-store, RR-Evict tail eviction, queue admission ordering, and block probation. No-store fails to distinguish reusable and one-use segments within a request; a capacity-matched CPU replay is its cheapest falsifier. Tail eviction cannot prevent pollution before reclamation; the same replay compares its recomputed tokens. Queue ordering needs eligible waiting peers and may delay cold requests; a scheduler replay checks both conditions. Retained probation with explicit ancestry, recomputation-based promotion, group commit, and async rollback rules.

hypotheses.title: Payback-gated expert-placement commits
hypotheses.mechanism: Keep a computed EPLB placement plan pending until recent rank skew is likely to repay migration and the serving state can tolerate the commit. Change the timing of weight movement and map publication, without changing the placement algorithm, token routing, or expert precision.
hypotheses.nearest_prior_art: Open #62009 adds asynchronous EPLB work, MegaMoE mapping fusion, and a migration backend; open #61839 adds a rebalance cap; open #59168 describes online placement and replica routing. These are direct controls. #62009's GB200 multi-node, decode-only result does not establish single-node B200 transfer.
hypotheses.new_adaptation: Add a pending-plan state and payback gate to the EPLB controller. The first implementation uses a quiescent all-rank serving boundary for in-place migration: drain in-flight forwards and graph replays, agree on plan version and source map, migrate weights, verify each rank's destination rows, then publish the new map version before serving resumes. Before any weight mutation, timeout safely discards or defers the plan and leaves the old map active. After mutation starts, a failed collective must fail closed and recover from a known placement or restart; it cannot claim to roll back merely by restoring the old map. Shadow slots are an optional alternative only if measured free HBM supports them.
hypotheses.code_surface: EPLB plan state, migration scheduler and communicator, per-rank weight/map version tracking, and the active MoE backend's map publication path. The pinned active backend and #62009 base/head are unresolved.
hypotheses.online_policy: Observable state: recent per-layer rank load and MoE step time, migration bytes and measured pause cost, queued prefills, active decodes, per-rank free HBM, and pending-plan age. Decision rule: at a safe boundary, commit only if estimated saved slow-rank time over a bounded horizon exceeds migration and queueing cost by a hysteresis margin; otherwise defer or discard at expiry. Action: either execute one versioned all-rank migration and publish the map, or keep the old placement. Overhead: host scoring, existing load collection, and measured coordination cost. Fallback: existing fixed placement or qualified async EPLB cadence. Strongest static comparator: best fixed placement and a capped rebalance schedule with equal expert memory.
hypotheses.strongest_objection: Single-node migration may be cheap enough that gating only prolongs imbalance, while quiescent in-place migration may stall serving and shadow migration may exceed HBM. #62009 already removes host work from the decode critical path. Durable rank skew, migration payback, and support in either B200 layout are unmeasured.

novelty.deployment: Unestablished for B200 DEP8 and two DEP4; reported #62009 gains use a different GB200 topology and decode-only workload.
novelty.implementation: Proposed timing gate and versioned commit protocol, conditional on the active backend and on a similar gate not already existing in the pinned tree.
novelty.publication: Unestablished; online expert placement and refresh already have close prior art.

hypotheses.confidence: Moderate in the migration-versus-skew tradeoff; low in target benefit.
hypotheses.readiness: Low. A host policy replay is straightforward, but safe migration integration requires backend and memory qualification.

evidence.quote: takes async EPLB's host work off the decode critical path
evidence.claim: Existing work already addresses a major source of EPLB overhead.

evidence.quote: Within one node, `symm_mem` and NIXL (CUDA IPC) move weights at a similar rate
evidence.claim: The reported cross-node migration advantage is not a single-node B200 prediction.

evidence.claim: Commit frequency and timing can affect service latency.

evidence.claim: A simple rebalance cap is a strong low-complexity comparator.

evidence.quote: Synchronous rearrangement dominates EPLB wall time
evidence.claim: Improved rank balance can still lose total throughput after migration.

evidence.quote: UltraEP's online refresh re-solves placement and per-replica quotas every N representative batches
evidence.claim: Placement refresh and replica routing are existing alternative mechanisms.

rubric.value: Conditional TPOT-tail and throughput opportunity if rank skew persists long enough to repay migration.
rubric.mechanism: Gate a prepared placement plan using measured migration cost, rank skew, queue pressure, and memory headroom.
rubric.evidence: Other deployments show both EPLB benefits and costly rearrangement; target transfer is unmeasured.
rubric.integration: Requires collective version agreement, quiescent migration or shadow storage, and active-backend support.
rubric.correctness: No forward may use a map version until all corresponding expert weights are valid on every rank; mid-migration failure must fail closed.
rubric.experiment: Start with a component comparison of rank skew, migration pause, and free HBM, then host policy replay; use serving A/B only if the payback case survives.
rubric.cost: Cheap host replay; multi-GPU correctness and matched serving work substantial and unestimated.
rubric.distinctness: Changes commit timing, rather than enabling EPLB, changing placement, or routing replicas per token.
rubric.research_contribution: A load-dependent commit policy may be useful; publication novelty unestablished.

experiment.control: EPLB off, best fixed placement, qualified existing async cadence, and a rebalance cap at equal redundant-expert memory.
experiment.treatment: Same placement algorithm and migration backend with only the pending-plan commit gate added.
experiment.measurements: Per-layer rank skew and MoE time, migration bytes and serving pause, per-rank free HBM, prefill queue delay, TTFT/TPOT tails, throughput, cost per token, and agent/tool quality at matched concurrency on DEP8 and two DEP4.
experiment.reject_if: The component test finds no durable skew, insufficient HBM or migration payback, or matched serving loses to the best fixed/async/capped control.
experiment.correctness: Test plan-version agreement, idle and unequal DP batches, graph replay, no request admitted during in-place mutation, timeout before mutation, and fail-closed behavior after mutation. Compare expert outputs at fixed precision and evaluate agent/tool quality.
experiment.cost: Component measurement and host replay first; serving duration and setup remain unknown. No GPU work was performed.

hypotheses.revision_after_critique: Explored enabling existing EPLB, a fixed rebalance cap, per-token replica routing, and a payback-gated commit. EPLB activation is existing work; a component test of skew versus migration cost can falsify its value here. A cap is simpler but cannot react to changing load; a host cadence replay is its cheapest comparison. Replica routing overlaps #59168 and needs redundant capacity; a memory and routing component check can rule it out. Retained commit timing with a quiescent, versioned in-place protocol and safe defer/discard before mutation.
